A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DSpodFL research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–P. All 57 appendix pages match in text and rendered content after excluding page numbers; the shorter v4 reflects main-text reflow.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix O report original Fashion-MNIST/SVM and CIFAR10/VGG11 experiments, including accuracy-delay comparisons, numerical tables, and sensitivity analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and their outcomes in Section 5 and Appendix O, including Figures 2–11 and Tables 2–5.

M1.justification: The sporadic SGD and aggregation procedure, mixing weights, update equations in Section 3, and Algorithm 1 in Appendix B are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Fashion-MNIST and CIFAR10 image classification under the same IID/non-IID distributions and resource scenarios, including time-varying probabilities and alternative resource distributions in Appendix O.

E2.justification: The corresponding empirical comparisons retain DGD, Randomized Gossip, Sporadic SGDs, and DFedAvg. The removed background citations do not remove any evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: Section 5 retains the same models, data assignments, delay metric, default 10-client graph with radius 0.4, learning rate 0.01, and batch size 16. Appendix O's experimental protocols also match.

E4.justification: The analyses of data/resource heterogeneity, graph connectivity, client count, dynamic probabilities, learning-rate sensitivity, and processing/transmission delay decomposition are retained without changes in Figures 3–11 and Appendix O.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments are run multiple times and report means and one-sigma standard deviations. Neither changes the run-count or seed disclosures, uncertainty procedure, or reporting practice.

E6.justification: The numerical tables, plotted results, and reported findings are unchanged. For example, Table 4 retains DSpodFL's FMNIST overall delays of 1487.00 at IID accuracy 0.75 and 688.65 at non-IID accuracy 0.40.

T1.justification: Section 4.4's 'Effects of sporadicity terms' discussion removes the trailing '= 1' from d_min = min d_i^(k), making a local mathematical correction. The formal assumptions, theorem statements, convergence bounds, and appendix proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: jointly modeling sporadic computations and communications, subsuming existing DFL methods, establishing convergence guarantees, and improving accuracy versus delay.

C2.justification: The resource-availability explanation, convergence-versus-delay tradeoff, explanation of lower accuracy at some fixed iterations, and limitation to the evaluated image-classification tasks remain substantively unchanged. The local equality correction is recorded under T1.

D1.justification: Both retain the same algorithm pseudocode, hyperparameters, three NVIDIA A100 GPUs with 40GB memory, and statement that training/testing code is provided in supplementary material. No implementation or access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: v4 removes McMahan et al. (2017) and Stich (2018) from Section 2 and the bibliography. It also drops local citations to Wang and Joshi (2018) and Zehtabi et al. (2022), while retaining those works elsewhere. The principal novelty positioning and Table 1 comparison remain unchanged.

P1.justification: Several contribution, related-work, theoretical-discussion, experimental-discussion, and conclusion passages are shortened. v4 adds a funding acknowledgment before the reproducibility statement. The main section sequence and appendix organization are retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 10 to page 9, Figures 3–4 shift within page 10, and mathematical displays and surrounding text are compacted and reflowed. Figure content, captions, and table structures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Removing the potentially misleading '= 1' in Section 4.4 improves consistency with the general minimum-probability definition, while modest prose tightening and the funding acknowledgment improve presentation and disclosure. Background citation coverage is slightly reduced, but the principal comparisons remain supported. The overall gain is limited; the scientific evidence and proofs are unchanged.
